claim: HER2-positive breast cancer accounts for 15–20% of all breast cancer cases.
source: Accounting for 15–20% of all breast cancer cases, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) positive breast cancer has posed great threats to the health of women worldwide (Giaquinto et al., 2022; Harbeck et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Giaquinto et al., 2022; Harbeck et al., 2019).

claim: The overexpression of HER2 results in aberrant breast cancer cell proliferation, invasion, and progression.
source: The overexpression of HER2 results in aberrant breast cancer cell proliferation, invasion, and progression (Swain et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Swain et al., 2023).

claim: Trastuzumab has been recognized as the foundational medication in HER2-positive breast cancer treatment.
source: As a monoclonal antibody targeting HER2, trastuzumab has been recognized as the foundational medication in HER2-positive breast cancer treatment and provided remarkable clinical benefits for numerous patients (Marra et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Marra et al., 2024).

claim: Around 50% HER2-positive breast cancer patients would experience trastuzumab resistance and disease progression during or after treatment settings.
source: Around 50% HER2-positive breast cancer patients would experience trastuzumab resistance and disease progression during or after treatment settings (Cossetti et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Cossetti et al., 2015).

claim: Trastuzumab resistance mainly results from HER2 mutation, antigenic epitope variation, compensatory pathway activation, and tumor heterogeneity.
source: Current theories maintained that trastuzumab resistance mainly resulted from HER2 mutation (Xu et al., 2017), antigenic epitope variation (Arribas et al., 2011), compensatory pathway activation (Baselga et al., 2014) and tumor heterogeneity (Marchiò et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature (Xu et al., 2017; Arribas et al., 2011; Baselga et al., 2014; Marchiò et al., 2021).

claim: Metabolic reprogramming has been acknowledged as one crucial cancer hallmark.
source: Metabolic reprogramming has been acknowledged as one crucial cancer hallmark (Hanahan, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Hanahan, 2022).

claim: Glycolysis, TCA cycle, lipid metabolism, and amino acid metabolism collectively modulate the development and function of cancer cells and tumor microenvironment components.
source: Traced back to the first study carried out by Otto Warburg, decades of studies have indicated that glycolysis, tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, lipid metabolism, amino acid metabolism, as well as other processes collectively modulate the development and function of cancer cells and tumor microenvironment (TME) components (Martínez-Reyes and Chandel, 2021; Vander Heiden and DeBerardinis, 2017; Kao et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Martínez-Reyes and Chandel, 2021; Vander Heiden and DeBerardinis, 2017; Kao et al., 2022).

claim: Different breast cancer subtypes feature diverse metabolic patterns.
source: Several studies have revealed that different breast cancer subtypes featured diverse metabolic patterns (Gong et al., 2021; Xiao et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Gong et al., 2021; Xiao et al., 2022).

claim: Targeting specific enzymes or modulating nutrient uptake might normalize the TME and enhance breast cancer treatment efficacy.
source: Targeting specific enzymes or modulating nutrient uptake might normalize the TME and enhance breast cancer treatment efficacy (Miller et al., 2023; Xiao et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Miller et al., 2023; Xiao et al., 2023) and involves speculative reasoning about potential therapeutic approaches.

claim: Epigenetic modifications play crucial roles in all stages of cancer development and contribute to cancer cell survival selection.
source: Epigenetic modifications play crucial roles in all stages of cancer development and contribute to cancer cell survival selection (Timp and Feinberg, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Timp and Feinberg, 2013).

claim: Alterations in chromatin structure, DNA methylation, and histone modifications provide a tumor growth advantage and increase phenotypic variability.
source: Alterations in chromatin structure, DNA methylation, and histone modifications provide a tumor growth advantage and increase phenotypic variability (Feinberg et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Feinberg et al., 2016).

claim: Epigenetic dysregulation modulates key genes transcription associated with treatment tolerance, leading to resistant clonal derivatives and disease progression.
source: During the formation of drug resistance, epigenetic dysregulation modulates key genes transcription associated with treatment tolerance, leading to resistant clonal derivatives and disease progression (Brown et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Brown et al., 2014).

claim: COMPASS complex inactivation suppressed tumor suppressor genes transcription and accelerated breast cancer tumorigenesis.
source: Previous studies suggested that COMPASS complex inactivation suppressed tumor suppressor genes transcription and accelerated breast cancer tumorigenesis (Langille et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Langille et al., 2022).

claim: Aberrant DNA methylation resulted in abnormal oncogenic signaling activation and drug resistance acquisition.
source: Aberrant DNA methylation resulted in abnormal oncogenic signaling activation and drug resistance acquisition (Garcia-Martinez et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Garcia-Martinez et al., 2021).

claim: 203 metabolites (130 upregulated and 73 downregulated) were identified with different abundances between trastuzumab-sensitive and primary-resistant patient groups.
source: Of them, 203 metabolites (130 upregulated and 73 downregulated in primary-resistant groups) were identified with different abundances among two patient groups (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental metabolomics data presented in the manuscript and referenced figures.

claim: Glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism, valine, leucine, and isoleucine biosynthesis, as well as cysteine and methionine metabolism, were reduced in primary-resistant patients.
source: KEGG-based pathway analyses suggested the major enrichment in amino acid metabolism. For instance, glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism, valine, leucine, and isoleucine biosynthesis, as well as cysteine and methionine metabolism, were reduced in primary-resistant patients; while arginine, proline, alanine, aspartate, and glutamate metabolism were enhanced (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by pathway analysis of metabolomics data presented in the manuscript and referenced figures.

claim: Cystine and aspartate were higher in primary-resistant groups, while valine, lysine, and leucine were lower.
source: By comparing the abundance of 20 common protein-construction amino acids, we realized that cystine and aspartate were higher, while valine, lysine, and leucine were lower in primary-resistant groups. However, glutamate kept stable in both groups (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental metabolomics data comparing amino acid abundances between patient groups.

claim: 1542 genes were upregulated and 1350 genes were downregulated in non-pCR groups compared to pCR groups in the I-SPY2 trial.
source: By comparing patients with different responses to neoadjuvant trastuzumab-based regimens (pathological complete response [pCR] and non-pCR), we found 1542 genes upregulated and 1350 genes downregulated in non-pCR groups (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic analysis of the I-SPY2 trial data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Amino acid metabolism was found dysregulated in patients with poor responses to trastuzumab, including aberrant lysine degradation, cysteine and methionine metabolism, beta-alanine metabolism, and histidine metabolism.
source: Based on KEGG datasets, amino acid metabolism was found dysregulated in patients with poor responses to trastuzumab, including aberrant lysine degradation, cysteine and methionine metabolism, beta-alanine metabolism, and histidine metabolism (Figure 1H).
evidence: The claim is supported by pathway analysis of transcriptomic data from the I-SPY2 trial.

claim: Patients with non-pCR featured higher expression of SLC7A11, while no differences were found in GPX4, GSS, and GSR expression.
source: As cystine was one of the most significant amino acids in both metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses, we investigated relations between cystine/cysteine metabolic key genes and trastuzumab treatment outcomes. Patients with non-pCR featured higher expression of SLC7A11, while no differences were found in GPX4, GSS, and GSR expression (Figure 1I), indicating SLC7A11 might become a potential target for trastuzumab primary-resistant patients.
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic data analysis comparing gene expression between pCR and non-pCR patients.

claim: 181 upregulated and 235 downregulated hydrophilic metabolites accompany 546 upregulated and 412 downregulated lipophilic metabolites were found in JIMT1 cells compared to SKBR3 cells.
source: Specifically, 181 upregulated and 235 downregulated hydrophilic metabolites accompany 546 upregulated and 412 downregulated lipophilic metabolites were found in JIMT1 cells compared to SKBR3 cells (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolomics data comparing JIMT1 and SKBR3 cell lines.

claim: Glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism were upregulated in JIMT1, while cysteine and methionine metabolism were downregulated.
source: For hydrophilic metabolites, enrichment analyses revealed that glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism were upregulated in JIMT1, while cysteine and methionine metabolism were downregulated (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by pathway enrichment analysis of metabolomics data from cell lines.

claim: 4235 downregulated genes and 4923 upregulated genes were identified in the comparison between JIMT1 and SKBR3 cells.
source: Differential gene expression could also be uncovered from transcriptomic data. 4235 downregulated genes and 4923 upregulated genes were identified in the comparison between JIMT1 and SKBR3 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptomic analysis comparing JIMT1 and SKBR3 cell lines.

claim: Activities of cysteine and glutathione metabolism pathways were found dysregulated in JIMT1 cells.
source: Based on KEGG datasets, activities of cysteine and glutathione metabolism pathways were found dysregulated in JIMT1 cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by pathway analysis of transcriptomic data from cell lines.

claim: Joint pathway analyses combining metabolomic and transcriptomic data indicated that JIMT1 featured aberrant glutathione metabolism.
source: More importantly, the joint pathway analyses combining metabolomic and transcriptomic data indicated that JIMT1 featured aberrant glutathione metabolism (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by integrated analysis of metabolomics and transcriptomics data.

claim: JIMT1 cells showed higher cysteine uptake ability and cytoplasmic cysteine level but lower GSH/GSSG ratio than SKBR3 cells.
source: These altered peaks primarily located among the promoter regions of genes (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), which have close relationships with biological processes such as nucleic acid transcription, protein modification, mRNA processing, and ribosome processing (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of cysteine uptake, intracellular cysteine levels, and GSH/GSSG ratio in cell lines.

claim: Knockdown of SLC7A11 and GPX4 increased lipid peroxidation in JIMT1 cells.
source: We first downregulated the expression of SLC7A11 and GPX4 in JIMT1 by siRNAs, and the lipid peroxidation of ferroptosis was found to increase by measuring BODIPY-C11 (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing increased lipid peroxidation following siRNA-mediated knockdown.

claim: JIMT1 was more sensitive to SLC7A11 inhibitor (erastin) and GPX4 inhibitor (RSL3) than SKBR3.
source: We then detected the sensitivity of JIMT1 and SKBR3 to SLC7A11 inhibitor (erastin) and GPX4 inhibitor (RSL3) and found JIMT1 was more sensitive to these two inhibitors (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing drug sensitivity between cell lines.

claim: JIMT1 showed more tolerance to cysteine starvation than SKBR3.
source: The deprivation of cysteine could suppress the growth of both JIMT1 and SKBR3, but JIMT1 showed more tolerance to this nutritional starvation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing cell growth under cysteine starvation conditions.

claim: Treatment with erastin, RSL3, and cysteine starvation for 12 hr induced ferroptosis in both JIMT1 and SKBR3 cells.
source: 12 hr treatment of SLC7A11 inhibitor (erastin), GPX4 inhibitor (RSL3), and even cysteine starvation were all able to induce ferroptosis in both JIMT1 and SKBR3 cells (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing ferroptosis induction following various treatments.

claim: JIMT1 cells indicated more rapid accumulation of lipid peroxidation under the treatment of erastin than SKBR3.
source: However, JIMT1 cells indicated more rapid accumulation of lipid peroxidation under the treatment of erastin, which could be detected by both increased BODIPY-C11 and DCFH-DA (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of lipid peroxidation markers in cell lines treated with erastin.

claim: With prolonged exposure of trastuzumab for 72 hr, the total amount of SLC7A11 in JIMT1 was decreased.
source: We found that with a prolonged exposure of trastuzumab for 72 hr, the total amount of SLC7A11 in JIMT1 was decreased (Figure 3I).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing SLC7A11 protein levels after trastuzumab treatment.

claim: Cystine uptake ability was suppressed after trastuzumab treatment for 48 and 72 hr.
source: Correspondingly, cystine uptake ability was suppressed after trastuzumab treatment for 48 and 72 hr (Figure 3J).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of cystine uptake following trastuzumab treatment.

claim: Cells that underwent trastuzumab treatment combined with erastin or cysteine starvation demonstrated stronger lipid peroxidation and enhanced ferroptosis.
source: In addition, cells that underwent trastuzumab treatment combined with erastin or cysteine starvation could demonstrate stronger lipid peroxidation and enhanced ferroptosis (Figure 3K).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing synergistic effects of combination treatments on lipid peroxidation.

claim: Trastuzumab plus erastin and trastuzumab plus cysteine starvation could effectively inhibit tumor growth in JIMT1 xenograft mouse models.
source: Of them, trastuzumab plus erastin and trastuzumab plus cysteine starvation could effectively inhibit tumor growth, while cysteine starvation and erastin monotherapy only showed limited effects on tumor progression, demonstrating the better treatment responses of the combination strategy (Figure 4B and C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo experimental data from xenograft mouse models.

claim: Almost no weight differences were observed among all treatment groups during treatment.
source: In addition, almost no weight differences were observed among all groups during treatment, partially indicating the safety of such cysteine limitation treatment (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of mouse body weight during treatment.

claim: The infiltration of NK cells in tumors was increased only upon the combination of cysteine deprivation and trastuzumab.
source: The infiltration of NK cells (CD3-CD45+CD49b+) in tumors was increased only upon the combination of cysteine deprivation and trastuzumab (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of tumor-infiltrating immune cells.

claim: Nearly no differences were found in tumor-infiltrating NK cell activation, toxic function, and maturation status among all treatment groups.
source: Nearly no differences were found in tumor-infiltrating NK cell activation (NKp46), toxic function (Granzyme B), and maturation status (CD11b, CD27) among all these groups (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of NK cell markers in tumor samples.

claim: Erastin and cysteine deprivation monotherapy, or combined with trastuzumab, could upregulate SLC7A11 and GPX4 expression, as well as the abundance of MDA and 4-HNE.
source: Erastin and cysteine deprivation monotherapy, or combined with trastuzumab, could upregulate SLC7A11 and GPX4 expression, as well as the abundance of MDA and 4-HNE.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis of tumor samples from different treatment groups.

claim: 3934 and 3925 H3K4me3 peaks were enriched in JIMT1 and SKBR3, respectively.
source: By comparing the ChIP-seq data, we detected 3934 and 3925 H3K4me3 peaks were enriched in JIMT1 and SKBR3, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis comparing histone modifications between cell lines.

claim: H3K4me3 peaks primarily located among the promoter regions of genes.
source: These altered peaks primarily located among the promoter regions of genes (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), which have close relationships with biological processes such as nucleic acid transcription, protein modification, mRNA processing, and ribosome processing (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis showing genomic distribution of H3K4me3 peaks.

claim: 7048 and 7001 H3K27me3 peaks were enriched in JIMT1 and SKBR3, respectively.
source: We also confirmed that 7048 and 7001 H3K27me3 peaks were enriched in JIMT1 and SKBR3, respectively, mainly enriching at not only promoter regions but also distal intergenic regions, and exons (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) of genes that are involved in cell-cell adhesions, axon guidance, postsynaptic transmission, and neuron differentiation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis comparing H3K27me3 modifications between cell lines.

claim: The enrichment of H3K4me3 at the promoter regions of SLC7A11 was found in JIMT1 cells compared with SKBR3 cells, while H3K27me3 signals were stable.
source: Particularly, we uncovered the enrichment of H3K4me3 at the promoter regions of key cysteine transporter gene SLC7A11 in JIMT1 cells compared with SKBR3 cells, while H3K27me3 signals were stable (Figure 5C), showing the consistency with its high expression in JIMT1 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis of histone modifications at the SLC7A11 promoter.

claim: Inhibiting ASH2L downregulated the overall H3K4me3 level and the signal at SLC7A11 promoter in JIMT1 cells, and decreased the expression of SLC7A11.
source: By inhibiting the expression of ASH2L, one crucial subunit of COMPASS complex (Piunti and Shilatifard, 2016), we downregulated not only the overall H3K4me3 level but also the signal at SLC7A11 promoter in JIMT1 cells, and successfully decreased the expression of SLC7A11 (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of ASH2L knockdown on H3K4me3 levels and SLC7A11 expression.

claim: Diminished downstream cysteine uptake led to increased lipid peroxidation following ASH2L inhibition.
source: Meanwhile, diminished downstream cysteine uptake led to increased lipid peroxidation, the key symbol of ferroptosis (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements of cysteine uptake and lipid peroxidation following ASH2L knockdown.

claim: JIMT1 cells featured a lower abundance of total 5-mC than SKBR3 cells.
source: In general, JIMT1 cells featured a lower abundance of total 5-mC than SKBR3 cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by dot blot analysis of total DNA methylation levels.

claim: 329419 CG-DMRs were enriched in JIMT1 and 84634 CG-DMRs were enriched in SKBR3.
source: By investigating DNA methylation landscape with WGBS, we identified 329419 CG-DMRs enriched in JIMT1 and 84634 CG-DMRs enriched in SKBR3 (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by whole-genome bisulfite sequencing data analysis.

claim: The CpG methylation at SLC7A11 promoter region was decreased in JIMT1 compared with SKBR3.
source: SLC7A11 is located at chromosome 4q28.3 and we found that, in comparison with SKBR3, the CpG methylation at SLC7A11 promoter region was decreased in JIMT1 (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by WGBS data analysis of DNA methylation at the SLC7A11 promoter.

claim: dCas9-DNMT3A together with SLC7A11-specific promoter-targeting sgRNA successfully increased the 5-mC level at SLC7A11 promoter regions in JIMT1 cells.
source: To further verify the influence of altered promoter CG-DMR on SLC7A11 gene transcription, CRISPR/Cas9-based genomic editing tool dCas9-DNMT3A together with SLC7A11-specific promoter-targeting sgRNA sets were utilized to successfully increase the 5-mC level at SLC7A11 promoter regions (Figure 6C) in JIMT1 cells, which is confirmed by MeDIP-qPCR (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data using CRISPR-based epigenetic editing and MeDIP-qPCR validation.

claim: Increased DNA methylation at SLC7A11 promoter reduced the expression of SLC7A11 and cysteine uptake, and stimulated cellular lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis in JIMT1 cells.
source: As a result, the expression of SLC7A11 and cysteine uptake were reduced (Figure 6E and F), and the following cellular lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis were stimulated in JIMT1 cells (Figure 6G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of targeted DNA methylation on gene expression, cysteine uptake, and ferroptosis.

claim: Cysteine is mainly obtained from dietary, protein catabolism, and methionine transsulfuration.
source: Cysteine is a crucial non-essential amino acid and mainly obtained from dietary, protein catabolism, and methionine transsulfuration (Bonifácio et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Bonifácio et al., 2021) and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Cystine, instead of cysteine, is normally taken in by the major transporter SLC7A11 due to oxidative extracellular environment.
source: Due to oxidative extracellular environment, cystine, instead of cysteine, is normally taken in by the major transporter SLC7A11 (also known as xCT) (Koppula et al., 2021), which also has important roles in protein synthesis, posttranslational modifications, and redox balance maintenance (Bonifácio et al., 2021; Lennicke and Cochemé, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Koppula et al., 2021; Bonifácio et al., 2021; Lennicke and Cochemé, 2021) and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Biosynthesis of GSH by GSS is one important outlet of cellular cysteine, which helps maintaining oxidation-reduction balance and protecting membrane from oxidative damage including ferroptosis with GPX4 and GSR.
source: Meanwhile, biosynthesis of GSH by GSS is one important outlet of cellular cysteine, which helps maintaining oxidation-reduction balance and protecting membrane from oxidative damage including ferroptosis with GPX4 and GSR (Sies et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Sies et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2024) and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: SLC7A11 inhibition, cysteine deprivation, or targeting GPX4 have been reported to effectively enhance lipid peroxidation and induce ferroptosis in several cancer types.
source: As an important rate-limiting metabolite of the GSH biosynthesis, cysteine modulates ferroptosis through the cyst(e)ine/GSH/GPX4 axis (Stockwell, 2022). SLC7A11 inhibition, cysteine deprivation, or targeting GPX4 have been reported to effectively enhance lipid peroxidation and induce ferroptosis in several cancer types (Dixon et al., 2012; Badgley et al., 2020; Shi et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Stockwell, 2022; Dixon et al., 2012; Badgley et al., 2020; Shi et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2023).

claim: The inhibition of HER2 could result in impaired redox homeostasis and increased ROS.
source: The inhibition of HER2 could result in impaired redox homeostasis and increased ROS (Fox et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Fox et al., 2020).

claim: Tumor cells might adapt to metabolic stress by activating antioxidant signaling pathways and acquire recurrence and dormancy.
source: Tumor cells might adapt to this metabolic stress by activating antioxidant signaling pathways and acquire recurrence and dormancy (Fox et al., 2020; Parida et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Fox et al., 2020; Parida et al., 2022) and involves speculative reasoning about tumor adaptation mechanisms.

claim: The anti-tumor effects of trastuzumab mainly relies on antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) effects mediated by NK cells.
source: As the anti-tumor effects of trastuzumab mainly relies on antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) effects mediated by NK cells (Musolino et al., 2022), this combination therapy might provide more effective approaches for HER2-positive breast cancer treatment.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Musolino et al., 2022) and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Ferroptosis might increase endoplasmic reticulum stress and activate p53 upregulated modulator of apoptosis (PUMA).
source: Ferroptosis might increase endoplasmic reticulum stress and activate p53 upregulated modulator of apoptosis (PUMA) (Lee et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Lee et al., 2020) and involves speculative reasoning about ferroptosis mechanisms.

claim: Altered methylations on promoter histone H3K4 and H3K27 show the most important effects on gene expression.
source: Abnormal changes of histone modification play critical roles in tumor progression, including drug resistance (Jin and Jeong, 2023). Of them, altered methylations on promoter histone H3K4 and H3K27 show the most important effects on gene expression (Millán-Zambrano et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Jin and Jeong, 2023; Millán-Zambrano et al., 2022) and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: MLL mutations were identified among various cancers and widespread shortening H3K4me3 peaks at tumor suppressor genes might contribute to tumor initiation.
source: Several studies have described the regulatory roles of histone modifications on oncogene transcription (Wang et al., 2023b; Sun et al., 2022). MLL mutations were identified among various cancers and widespread shortening H3K4me3 peaks at tumor suppressor genes might contribute to tumor initiation (Zhao et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2015), and H3K27me3 could modulate chemotherapy tolerance in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) (Marsolier et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Wang et al., 2023b; Sun et al., 2022; Zhao et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2015) and involves speculative reasoning about tumor initiation mechanisms.

claim: H3K27me3 could modulate chemotherapy tolerance in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).
source: MLL mutations were identified among various cancers and widespread shortening H3K4me3 peaks at tumor suppressor genes might contribute to tumor initiation (Zhao et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2015), and H3K27me3 could modulate chemotherapy tolerance in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) (Marsolier et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Marsolier et al., 2022).

claim: The combination of chemotherapy and H3K27me3 demethylation inhibitor could prevent the proliferation of persister cells.
source: Moreover, the combination of chemotherapy and H3K27me3 demethylation inhibitor could prevent the proliferation of persister cells (Marsolier et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Marsolier et al., 2022).

claim: Targeting KDM6A could inhibit JIMT1 tumor growth via decreasing tRNA transcription.
source: Targeting KDM6A could inhibit JIMT1 tumor growth via decreasing tRNA transcription (Duan et al., 2024b).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Duan et al., 2024b).

claim: Almost all cancers feature abnormal DNA hypomethylation and local hypermethylation at specific CpG islands compared with normal tissues.
source: Compared with normal tissues, almost all cancers feature abnormal DNA hypomethylation and local hypermethylation at specific CpG islands (Zhao et al., 2021; Nishiyama and Nakanishi, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Zhao et al., 2021; Nishiyama and Nakanishi, 2021) and represents established scientific knowledge.

claim: Dysregulated DNA methylation contributes to breast cancer tumorigenesis and drug resistance formation.
source: Dysregulated DNA methylation contributes to breast cancer tumorigenesis and drug resistance formation (Sher et al., 2022; Sukocheva et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Sher et al., 2022; Sukocheva et al., 2022).

claim: Trastuzumab-resistant HER2-positive breast cancer was found associated with downregulated TGFBI, CXCL2, and SLC38A1, which was silenced by DNA hypermethylation.
source: For instance, trastuzumab-resistant HER2-positive breast cancer was found associated with downregulated TGFBI, CXCL2, and SLC38A1, which was silenced by DNA hypermethylation (Palomeras et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Palomeras et al., 2019).

claim: Aberrant DNMT1, DNMT3A, and DNMT3B expression were correlated with endocrine therapy resistance and predicted worsened pathologic status and prognosis.
source: Aberrant DNMT1, DNMT3A, and DNMT3B expression were correlated with endocrine therapy resistance and predicted worsened pathologic status and prognosis (Jahangiri et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Jahangiri et al., 2019).

claim: Increased H3K4me3 might interact with DNMT3A-DNMT3L.
source: What's more, since increased H3K4me3 might interact with DNMT3A-DNMT3L (Du et al., 2015), the crosstalk between histone modification and DNA methylation may have collaborative effects on cysteine metabolism in trastuzumab primary-resistant breast cancer.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature (Du et al., 2015) and involves speculative reasoning about epigenetic crosstalk.

claim: The crosstalk between histone modification and DNA methylation may have collaborative effects on cysteine metabolism in trastuzumab primary-resistant breast cancer.
source: What's more, since increased H3K4me3 might interact with DNMT3A-DNMT3L (Du et al., 2015), the crosstalk between histone modification and DNA methylation may have collaborative effects on cysteine metabolism in trastuzumab primary-resistant breast cancer.
evidence: The claim involves speculative reasoning based on inference from the interaction between H3K4me3 and DNMT3A-DNMT3L.

claim: The study integrated metabolomics, transcriptomics, and epigenomics data of trastuzumab-sensitive and primary-resistant HER2-positive breast cancer to identify metabolic alterations.
source: Here, we integrated metabolomics, transcriptomics, and epigenomics data of trastuzumab-sensitive and primary-resistant HER2-positive breast cancer to identify metabolic alterations.
evidence: The claim describes the study design and methodology, which is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Aberrant cysteine metabolism was discovered in trastuzumab primary-resistant breast cancer at both circulating and intracellular levels.
source: Aberrant cysteine metabolism was discovered in trastuzumab primary-resistant breast cancer at both circulating and intracellular levels.
evidence: The claim is supported by metabolomics data from patient plasma samples and cell line experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: The inhibition of SLC7A11 and cysteine starvation could synergize with trastuzumab to induce ferroptosis.
source: The inhibition of SLC7A11 and cysteine starvation could synergize with trastuzumab to induce ferroptosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro and in vivo studies showing synergistic effects of combination treatments.

claim: Increased H3K4me3 and decreased DNA methylation enhanced SLC7A11 transcription and cystine uptake in trastuzumab-resistant breast cancer.
source: Mechanistically, increased H3K4me3 and decreased DNA methylation enhanced SLC7A11 transcription and cystine uptake in trastuzumab-resistant breast cancer.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq, WGBS, and functional validation experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: The regulation of epigenetic modifications modulated cysteine metabolism and ferroptosis sensitivity.
source: The regulation of epigenetic modifications modulated cysteine metabolism and ferroptosis sensitivity.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing effects of epigenetic manipulation on cysteine metabolism and ferroptosis.

claim: The patient cohort consists of 26 primary trastuzumab-resistant patients defined as disease recurrence during or after (≤12 mo) trastuzumab adjuvant treatment and 26 trastuzumab-sensitive patients that benefited from trastuzumab adjuvant treatment more than 12 mo.
source: One breast cancer patient cohort from Jiangsu Province Hospital was embedded in this study, which consists of 26 primary trastuzumab-resistant patients defined as disease recurrence during or after (≤12 mo) trastuzumab adjuvant treatment and 26 trastuzumab-sensitive patients that benefited from trastuzumab adjuvant treatment more than 12 mo (Wong et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim describes the patient cohort used in the study, which is supported by the study design and methodology.
